artist.name: Caleb Hearn
artist.place_of_origin: Mount Airy, North Carolina, United States
artist.short_description: North Carolina-born, Nashville-based singer-songwriter making personal, emotionally direct folk-pop and singer-songwriter pop.
artist.biography: Caleb Hearn is an American singer-songwriter from Mount Airy, North Carolina, who is based in Nashville, Tennessee. Growing up around family members who made music, he learned guitar as a child and developed an interest in writing songs. During the COVID-19 period, he reconsidered his direction as a musician, turning toward more personal material rather than chasing a particular commercial sound. His reworked 2020 release “Always Be 2.0,” drawn from grief after the death of a close friend, became a breakthrough with listeners online. In 2022, Hearn signed with Nettwerk and released “Where Do We Go from Here?,” a story inspired by a family he knew. His 2022 EP We’re Getting Older examined heartbreak and the effort to understand himself; 2023’s 1200 sq ft looked back at childhood and family life. His duet “Little Bit Better” with ROSIE arrived in 2024 and became one of his best-known recordings. That year also brought his debut studio album, Left on McKinney. In February 2026, he followed it with LEAVE THE WORLD BEHIND, a second album reflecting on change and moving forward. For Afterglow listeners, Hearn fits the intersection of confessional pop, folk-pop, and intimate singer-songwriter storytelling. That genre description is editorial, informed by published descriptions of his music, not a rigid official classification.
